scope: All seven tritiated-deoxycytidine source rows under the affected unlabeled dC structure, from PMID8244716 and PMID20681788, fixing the confirmed radiolabeled-to-unlabeled identity mismatch across doses and endpoint descriptions. Replacement audit additionally corrects four same-study amino-dideoxycytidine rows and one AzadC row, and excludes one nonhost-genome endpoint. Two ara-CTP records additionally receive verified covalent structure correction and L4 DNA-repair placement. Four DCTP pteridine same-paper records additionally receive verified identity correction from the full systematic name. Five further source rows correct CCMP/BPC material attribution and ADP identity or remove non-carcinogenic normal-tissue differentiation/erythropoiesis endpoints. Additional source-bound azacitidine identity/placement corrections and one QC-only exclusion cover the two exposed studies. The complete PMID171682 normal-erythropoiesis endpoint group is excluded across all 21 same-study rows, for positive and negative responses alike. One BDCA haloacetate source is reassigned from its false brominated-nucleoside identity. The four final observed replacement defects are repaired: two distinct CPC materials, a decitabine sub-G1 move to L3, and an unrelated annelid regeneration endpoint exclusion. Freeze this bounded batch for one replay; subsequent new replacement surfaces are inventoried for a later iteration, not automatically certified. Unrelated pending candidates are unchanged.
review_method: Codex record-by-record source-field audit, PubMed identity verification and available primary full texts; hash-bound corrections through shared overlay.
candidate_selection: R3 actual claims/new_evidence_assessment in valid317, then indexed siblings of four implicated structures. Explicit alternative-agent identity candidates checked; comparator-only matches excluded from decisions. Pre-inference replacement check also covers derivative-8/captopril and physiological-coupling siblings plus apoptosis misplacement.
limitations: Post-hoc inspected valid/test diagnostic. Other candidate cards and unresolved acronym identities are not certified clean. Gold/L1 and round3 endpoint selection are unchanged.

decisions.reason: The assay measures proliferation of contact-inhibited WB-F344 cells after treatment; increased cell number beyond the contact-inhibited control directly reflects loss of intercellular growth restraint, which is an L6 epigenetic/intercellular growth-restraint endpoint. This is not a tumor bioassay but is a valid cancer-relevant mechanism record.
Retain mixed L2 card: the complete support/context also contains an agent-attributed overall tumor/carcinogenicity assertion; moving the entire card would move that assertion into a mechanism family.

The assay measures long-term expansion of normal human bronchial and prostate epithelial cells under TGF-beta inhibition, achieving >1,000,000-fold proliferation. This is a growth-escape/proliferation mechanism relevant to L3, not a tumor outcome or carcinogenicity bioassay. Co-treatment with Y-27632 is noted but does not invalidate the A83-01-attributed effect. Placement in L3 is defensible.

The card reports an in vivo rat bone-marrow chromosome aberration assay, which directly measures structural chromosome damage. This endpoint belongs in L4 regardless of the negative result. The negative finding is a valid observation and should not be excluded merely because it does not show an effect.

Frozen actual-voter membership: no automatic gold or L1 edit. Card reports lifetime oral carcinogenicity bioassays in rats and mice with an explicit negative carcinogenicity conclusion for eugenol. The listed tumor types are endpoint labels, not positive findings, and genotoxicity data are explicitly separated as non-carcinogenicity evidence. Placement as direct animal carcinogenicity evidence is appropriate.

Frozen actual-voter membership: no automatic gold or L1 edit. Card reports TCHQ as a tumor promoter in a DMBA-initiated CD-1 mouse skin initiation-promotion protocol, with a positive carcinogenicity conclusion. This is direct experimental tumor outcome evidence for the agent, appropriate for L1 carcinogenicity evidence. No attribution mismatch or irrelevant endpoint identified.

The card measures danazol-induced telomere elongation and hematologic recovery in bone marrow failure, not genotoxicity or DNA damage. This is receptor-mediated regenerative growth involving androgen-like signaling and telomerase regulation, fitting L7 injury-associated regeneration/receptor-driven proliferation. No tumor outcome is reported, so L2 is not appropriate; no DNA lesions or mutations are measured, so L4 is not appropriate. Keep as a valid receptor-mechanism record.

The card reports decreased staurosporine-induced apoptosis measured by DNA fragmentation in MCF-7 breast carcinoma cells. Apoptosis is explicitly listed as an L3 cancer-relevant endpoint, and decreased apoptosis supports survival/growth escape. Placement at level 3 is appropriate.

The card reports increased total F2-isoprostanes in SH-SY5Y cells after docetaxel exposure, a direct lipid peroxidation/oxidative injury endpoint. This fits L5 reactive metabolism/redox/oxidative injury. It is not a tumor outcome or genotoxicity endpoint, and the neuroblastoma cell system does not change the measured oxidative endpoint.

The card reports cell-free horseradish peroxidase/H2O2/GSH-mediated oxygen uptake and DMPO-trapped thiyl radical formation for benzidine. This is direct evidence of peroxidase-driven one-electron oxidation producing reactive sulfur/oxygen intermediates, matching L5 reactive metabolism, reactive intermediates, and oxidative injury. It is not a tumor outcome or genotoxicity endpoint, so L5 placement is appropriate.

The card reports increased TUNEL-positive apoptotic cells in 661W photoreceptor cells after atRAL exposure. Apoptosis is an explicit L3 cancer-relevant endpoint, so placement at level 3 is appropriate even though the evidence_family label mentions transformation/growth escape. This is not a tumor outcome or carcinogenicity bioassay, but it is a valid mechanistic apoptosis measurement and should remain at L3.

In vitro EdU proliferation assay in primary human VSMCs stimulated with PDGF; PAP-1 (Kv1.3 blocker) inhibits receptor-driven proliferation. This is a receptor-mediated growth/proliferation mechanism, fitting L7. It is not a carcinogenicity bioassay, but L7 includes such mechanistic growth endpoints; no attribution mismatch or irrelevant endpoint.

The card measures iron/ascorbate-induced lipoperoxidation of phosphatidylcholine vesicles and reports decreased MDA accumulation due to scavenging by the tested compound. This is a direct oxidative-injury/protection endpoint, consistent with L5 reactive metabolism/redox/oxidative injury/protection. It is not a carcinogenicity bioassay, but it is a valid mechanistic antioxidant observation and should remain at L5 rather than being excluded or moved.

This complete card reports a derived DNA-methylation aging/capacity clock in a metabolic clinical cohort, not a cancer-associated locus, malignant-growth epigenetic mechanism, transformation or tumor outcome. Preserve the clinical aging observation outside this carcinogenicity retrieval source; its increased/decreased/null clock result is not a carcinogenicity direction.

The card reports a direct in vitro proliferation assay in MCF7 breast cancer cells using [3H]thymidine incorporation, with no significant effect for TCPM. This is a valid negative cancer-cell proliferation observation and fits L3 transformation/growth/proliferation endpoints. No attribution mismatch or irrelevant endpoint is present.

The card reports a chromosome aberration assay in CHO cells with S9 metabolic activation, showing a weakly positive, dose-dependent increase in chromatid-type aberrations. This is a direct chromosome damage endpoint, correctly placed in L4 genotoxicity/DNA damage and repair.

Measured endpoint is MDA (malondialdehyde) in lung homogenate, a lipid peroxidation/oxidative injury marker. Losartan reduced bleomycin-elevated MDA in a dose-related manner, so the record is a redox/oxidative protection observation, not a tumor outcome or genotoxicity endpoint. This fits L5 reactive metabolism/oxidative injury/protection; no need to move or exclude.

The card reports direct measurement of PhIP-DNA adducts by 32P-postlabeling in rat hepatocytes, with GSH depletion increasing adduct formation and UDS. This is a covalent DNA adduct endpoint, squarely within L4 genotoxicity/DNA damage. The tested entity matches the PhIP structure, and the GSH-depletion pretreatment is a mechanistic modifier rather than a different agent.

The card reports micronucleus formation after release from metaphase block in cultured mammalian cells, with spindle-fiber absence and C-mitosis indicating an aneugenic/spindle-poison mechanism. Micronuclei are explicitly listed under L4 chromosome damage endpoints, and the qualitative nature or joint reporting does not invalidate placement. No wrong-level or attribution issue is present.

The measured endpoint is induced micronucleus frequency in SCC VII tumor cells after TPZ with or without ZD6126. Micronucleus formation is chromosome damage/genotoxicity, which belongs in L4, not L2. The in vivo tumor-bearing system alone does not make it an overall tumor outcome because no tumor incidence, burden, growth, or agent-attributed carcinogenicity conclusion is reported. The modulation of TPZ-induced micronuclei by ZD6126 is a valid L4 genotoxicity finding.

The card reports intracellular ROS accumulation in a tumor cell line and its blockade by P450 inhibitors, with cell death mentioned only as supporting context. This is a redox/oxidative injury endpoint, not a tumor incidence, burden, growth, or carcinogenicity assertion. It therefore belongs in L5 (reactive metabolism/redox/oxidative injury) rather than L2.

The card reports an in vivo mouse spermatocyte chromosome aberration assay with a statistically significant increase in abnormal metaphases after amitriptyline exposure. This is a direct chromosome damage endpoint, correctly placed in L4 genotoxicity/DNA damage. No attribution mismatch or irrelevant endpoint is present.

The card reports inhibition of ROS production in activated human neutrophils, a direct redox/oxidative protection endpoint. This fits L5 reactive metabolism/redox/oxidative injury/protection. It is not a carcinogenicity bioassay, but L5 explicitly includes oxidative protection, so placement is appropriate.

The card measures TBARS (lipid peroxidation/oxidative stress) in rat tissue homogenates after DMH with/without RA. This is a redox/oxidative injury/protection marker, not a tumor outcome, mutation, or DNA-adduct endpoint. It belongs in L5 (reactive metabolism, redox/oxidative injury/protection). The protective-intervention design and missing numerical values do not change the mechanistic level; no attribution mismatch is apparent.
NOB in the SALI/CLP/Nrf2-Gpx4 experiment is nobiletin, not norbixin. Primary full text: https://pubs.rsc.org/en/content/articlehtml/2023/fo/d3fo01684f

The measured endpoint is γH2AX phosphorylation as a surrogate for DNA double-strand breaks and its reduction after Aβ42 challenge, with accelerated DNA repair. This is a DNA damage/DNA repair endpoint, not an epigenetic or intercellular growth-restraint mechanism. It belongs in L4 (DNA lesions/DNA repair) and should be retained as a valid protective/antigenotoxic observation rather than excluded.

Confirmed wrong test-article assignment: raw PMID 20303376 concerns 1,2,3-trichloropropane (NTP TR-384), but this card is attached to a different structure through an erroneous TCP expansion. Quarantine the incorrect molecule-record association, not the original study or its result. Applies to positive, negative and mechanistic passages alike. Supersedes earlier payload-only keep decisions where applicable.

The card reports kidney MDA, a lipid peroxidation marker, in a gentamicin nephrotoxicity model. DAPA reduced gentamicin-elevated MDA, representing oxidative injury/protection. This directly fits Level 5 reactive metabolism/redox oxidative injury/protection and is not a tumor outcome or genotoxicity endpoint, so current placement is appropriate.

The card reports IQ-DNA-base adducts detected by 32P-postlabeling in SHE cells with S9 activation. This is a direct DNA adduct/lesion measurement, which belongs in L4 (DNA lesions/adducts), not in reactive metabolism/oxidative injury. The finding is valid for DNA adduct formation and should not be excluded.

The card reports ranitidine-induced reduction of gastric mucosal lipid peroxidation (MDA) in an LPS/acid-injury rat model. This is a direct oxidative-injury/protection endpoint, matching the reactive metabolism/oxidative injury family. It is not a tumor outcome or genotoxicity assay, so L5 placement is appropriate; any carcinogenicity inference would be downstream and unsupported by this record.
Liver 8-OHdG is oxidative DNA damage; DEN tumor model is context, no tumor outcome for OX is reported.

The card reports raloxifene covalent binding to human liver microsomal protein and its attenuation by GSH, directly measuring reactive metabolite/protein adduct formation. This fits L5 reactive metabolism, protein adducts, and reactive intermediates. It is not a tumor outcome and should not be elevated to a higher level.

The card reports concentration- and time-dependent GSH depletion in rat hepatocytes, linked to quinoid oxidative bioactivation of DMA. This is a direct reactive-metabolism/oxidative-injury endpoint, matching L5. It is not a tumor outcome or genotoxicity endpoint, and the needs_more_context flag does not invalidate the measured mechanistic observation.

The measured endpoint is apoptotic morphology/apoptosis. Chromatin condensation or a nucleosomal DNA ladder is an apoptosis readout here, not an independent epigenetic-state assay. Place in L3, preserving the reported direction, tissue/challenge context and unresolved acronym identity. This placement decision does not certify agent identity or an overall carcinogenicity direction.

This complete card reports a derived DNA-methylation aging/capacity clock in a metabolic clinical cohort, not a cancer-associated locus, malignant-growth epigenetic mechanism, transformation or tumor outcome. Preserve the clinical aging observation outside this carcinogenicity retrieval source; its increased/decreased/null clock result is not a carcinogenicity direction.

BrdU labeling index in primary human hepatocytes is a direct proliferation/DNA-synthesis endpoint. The negative result for clofibric acid is a valid species-specific mechanistic observation relevant to liver tumor growth, not a tumor outcome. It fits the L3 proliferation/cell-cycle family; no move or exclusion is warranted.

The card reports an in vivo host-mediated bacterial reverse mutation assay for clonazepam, measuring His+ revertant frequency in Salmonella typhimurium hisG46. The result is negative with no dose-related increase, and the discussion explicitly concludes non-mutagenicity. This is a bacterial mutation endpoint, correctly placed in L4.

The card reports bisulfite sequencing of sperm DNA methylation at imprinted loci after gestational MXC exposure, with mixed-direction changes and partial transgenerational persistence. This is a direct epigenetic/DNA methylation endpoint, appropriately placed in L6. It is not a tumor outcome or carcinogenicity bioassay, but L6 explicitly covers epigenetic changes, so no relocation is needed.

The card reports a cell proliferation assay in three human tumor cell lines, measuring whether prasugrel metabolites increase proliferation above a serum-starved baseline. This is a valid negative cancer-cell proliferation/growth-escape observation and fits L3. It is not a carcinogenicity bioassay, but it is appropriately placed as mechanistic evidence rather than excluded.

The card reports DNA damage in rat hepatocytes with inverse GSH dependence, attributed to oxidative bioactivation. This is a direct DNA-damage endpoint, appropriately placed in L4 (DNA lesions/damage). The lack of a lesion-specific assay is noted as needs_more_context but does not invalidate the measured DNA damage endpoint.

Hold without mutation: source review does not establish a sufficiently clear exclusion. Preserve valid scoped/negative/mechanistic evidence; unresolved concerns remain in audit. Card reports levator ani myotrophic growth in an androgen anabolic assay, with no tumor outcome, injury context, or explicit cancer-relevant mechanism. Although anabolic steroids can act via androgen receptor, the supplied record only indexes muscle growth versus testosterone propionate and does not provide a bounded cancer-relevant growth mechanism required for L7. Ordinary hormone-growth phenotype without cancer link should be excluded.

Human epidemiological review explicitly attributes intracranial meningioma risk to prolonged medrogestone use (OR 3.5). This is an agent-attributed tumor outcome/assertion, appropriate for L2 overall tumor evidence rather than a mechanistic or genotoxicity endpoint.

Frozen actual-voter membership: no automatic gold or L1 edit. Direct animal carcinogenicity bioassay in female Osborne-Mendel rats with intrapulmonary implantation of phenanthrene produced a squamous cell carcinoma at the highest dose, with a positive carcinogenicity conclusion and relative potency estimate. A single tumor and high dose are valid positive observations, not grounds for exclusion or downgrading.
Existing family is defensible for this overlapping mitotic/growth endpoint; the model proposal does not establish a clear wrong-level error.

Full card measures cell growth/selectivity in cultured cells or receptor-linked crypt/villus growth, not tumor incidence or observed neoplastic growth. Preserve all null/positive results, co-treatment, source limits and unresolved acronym identity; placement review does not certify identity.
Retain growth inhibition with serotonin co-treatment; broad L3/L7 boundary is not forced without a stronger reason.

The card directly measures glutathione and cysteine conjugates of the oxidized reactive quinone-imine metabolite of DMAP in rat hepatocytes. The card reports increased gap-junction intercellular communication via calcein dye transfer after cAMP analog stimulation in IAR20 cells. The card measures inhibition of MCA-induced morphological transformation/focus formation in C3H/10T1/2 cells, an in vitro transformation endpoint rather than an overall tumor outcome or carcinogenicity assertion. Under the level definitions, transformation assays belong in L3, even though the effect is protective (decreased transformed foci). The valid negative/protective observation should be preserved and placed at L3.

Full card supports reactive_metabolism_oxidative_injury: Nrf2/HO-1 oxidative protection is explicitly measured in qualifying context; retain the useful mechanism rather than discard the dermatitis card.

The card reports an in-vivo hemoglobin sulfinic acid amide adduct formed from a reactive benzidine metabolite, not a tumor outcome or DNA adduct. Protein adducts and reactive metabolite evidence belong in L5, so placement at L2 is too high.

Hepatic protein carbonyl content is a direct oxidative protein damage endpoint, consistent with L5 reactive metabolism/oxidative injury. Prednisolone increased PCC 1.96-fold, while montelukast cotreatment reduced it; this is a valid oxidative injury observation, not a tumor outcome. Placement at L5 is appropriate.

The card reports a bacterial reverse mutation (Ames) assay in six Salmonella typhimurium strains, with a negative result (<4.9% mutation frequency). This is a direct bacterial gene mutation endpoint, correctly placed in L4 genotoxicity/DNA damage evidence. The negative finding is a valid observation and does not require exclusion or reclassification.

The card reports AhR-associated release from contact inhibition and increased proliferation in confluent hepatic oval stem cells, a bounded cancer-relevant growth mechanism. This fits L7 receptor-driven growth/proliferation. It is not a tumor outcome or genotoxicity endpoint, so L2/L4 placement would be inappropriate.

The card reports increased histone H4 K8 acetylation and increased H3 K18 acetylation with reduced HDAC1/HDAC2 in K562 cells. This is a direct chromatin-state/epigenetic modification endpoint, matching L6 epigenetic changes. Missing dose/duration and lack of persistence are optional details, not grounds for exclusion.

The card measures intracellular ROS generation by DMT in intact human oral keratinocytes using the DCFH-DA assay, with a marked increase versus control. This is a direct reactive-oxygen/oxidative-injury endpoint, matching L5 reactive metabolism and oxidative injury. It is not a tumor outcome or genotoxicity endpoint, so L5 placement is appropriate.

The card reports a negative in vitro micronucleus assay result for SC81458/SC83288, which directly measures clastogenic/mutagenic activity. Micronucleus induction is an L4 endpoint alongside chromosome damage and DNA lesions, so the existing genotoxicity_dna_damage_repair placement is appropriate. Missing cell line, S9, and schedule details are noted as needs_more_context but do not invalidate the negative observation or require reclassification.

Frozen actual-voter membership: no automatic gold or L1 edit. Hold without mutation: source review does not establish a sufficiently clear exclusion. Preserve valid scoped/negative/mechanistic evidence; unresolved concerns remain in audit. Human MR study reports a causal association between genetically predicted high pyroglutamine levels and esophageal cancer (limited/suspected), which is relevant direct evidence. However, the attached SMILES NC1CCC(=O)NC1=O appears to represent 3-aminopiperidine-2,6-dione rather than pyroglutamine (5-oxopyrrolidine-2-carboxamide); identity cannot be resolved from the card, so flag for review rather than exclude.

The card reports a direct negative result for B(e)P on gap junction permeability in DM15 transformed fibroblasts, which is a valid L6 intercellular growth-restraint endpoint. Negative observations are retained; the card does not claim universal safety. The entity-list mis-tag is explicitly clarified in the card, with B(e)P identified as benzo(e)pyrene, so placement is defensible.

The card reports an authoritative IARC Group 3 classification for benzo[g,h,i]perylene, i.e., not classifiable as to human carcinogenicity. This is an overall carcinogenicity conclusion/assertion, appropriate for L2. It is a valid negative/uncertain observation and should not be excluded merely because it does not demonstrate a tumor outcome.

The card reports increased MCF-7 breast cancer cell proliferation/viability by MTT at 0.01 µM, with the decrease at 1 µM statistically insignificant. This is a direct cancer-cell proliferation endpoint, correctly placed in L3 transformation/growth/escape. No attribution mismatch or irrelevant endpoint is present.

The card reports hepatic GSH content after repeated mebendazole treatment, a direct redox/oxidative-injury-related endpoint. The result is largely negative with one transient decrease, but a valid negative observation in this pathway belongs in L5 reactive metabolism/oxidative injury. No exclusion is warranted merely because the effect was limited or because GSH is a measured endpoint rather than the test entity.

The measured endpoint is covalent binding of benzo(a)pyrene metabolites to intracellular DNA, a direct DNA adduct/lesion readout. Although the study uses metabolic modifiers to probe activation, the outcome belongs with DNA adducts/lesions (L4) rather than reactive metabolism/protein adducts (L5). The modifier effects are valid mechanistic observations and should be preserved.
Enzyme-modified comet measures oxidative DNA lesions, not tumor occurrence.

The card reports a Drosophila sex-linked recessive lethal germline mutation assay, a direct in vivo mutagenicity endpoint. The positive feeding result is a valid L4 mutation observation even though injection retesting was negative and reciprocal translocation was negative; mixed results and missing dose details do not invalidate placement. This is not a tumor outcome and should remain in genotoxicity/DNA damage rather than higher levels.

This is receptor-driven (AT1) DNA synthesis/proliferation in normal vascular smooth muscle cells, not cancer-cell proliferation, transformation, or tumor outcome. It fits L7 receptor-driven growth/proliferation with a bounded AT1 mechanism better than L3. No attribution mismatch; SMILES matches candesartan. Valid protective/mechanistic observation, not exclusion.

The card reports inhibition of MeIQ-induced umuC/SOS induction via suppression of its metabolic activation, an antigenotoxic/protective metabolic mechanism rather than a direct tumor outcome or DNA-damage endpoint. In vitro E-screen measures estrogen-receptor-mediated proliferation; reported no effect at tested concentrations. The card reports direct DNA adduct formation in acellular calf thymus DNA after incubation with α-acetoxyNPIP, with adduct peaks detected by HPLC. This is a DNA lesion/adduct assay, correctly placed in L4 genotoxicity/DNA damage. No tumor outcome, transformation, or cancer-cell endpoint is claimed, so higher levels are not supported. The positive adduct detection is a valid L4 observation even without numeric quantification or controls.

The card reports an in vitro assay for Top1 cleavable complexes / DNA-protein crosslinks in carcinoma cells. The card reports a bacterial reverse mutation (Ames) result with exogenous metabolic activation, which is a direct L4 genotoxicity endpoint. The negative call is a valid observation and does not need exclusion; downstream reasoning should not overextend it to universal safety.

The card measures covalent binding of reactive IQ metabolites to hepatocyte macromolecules, a direct reactive-metabolism/adduct endpoint. This fits L5 reactive metabolism/protein adducts/reactive intermediates; it is not a tumor outcome or DNA-specific adduct assay.

decisions.reason: Retain verified dose-dependent cell survival/death in L3 while separating normal osteoclast differentiation. Do not equate live/dead staining with apoptosis-specific mechanism.
